description:
You are an environmental engineer at an urban planning and water resources consulting firm preparing a benefit analysis for the City of Muncie's White River Restoration Project. The project proposes river channel improvements (vegetation removal, bank stabilization, selective dredging) that would reduce the main channel's Manning's roughness coefficient. You must quantify the hydraulic benefit of this improvement using HEC-RAS.

A channel improvement specification has been placed at ~/Documents/channel_improvement_spec.txt. A terminal is open in the Muncie HEC-RAS project directory.

Your tasks:
1. Read the channel improvement specification.
2. Run a BASELINE simulation (existing conditions, Manning's n as currently set in Muncie.p04.tmp.hdf) and save the results. Extract: overall peak WSE, mean peak WSE, number of cells where WSE > 930 ft (inundated cells threshold), and total number of cells. Save these to ~/Documents/hec_ras_results/baseline_results.json.
3. Apply the channel improvement by modifying the Manning's n values in Muncie.p04.tmp.hdf using Python/h5py. The improvement spec defines the new n value for main-channel cells. Main-channel cells are those whose terrain elevation (Geometry/2D Flow Areas/Muncie/Cells Minimum Elevation) is in the lowest tercile of all cell elevations. Change ONLY those cells' Manning's n to the improved value; leave floodplain cells unchanged.
4. Run an IMPROVED CONDITIONS simulation and extract the same metrics. Save to ~/Documents/hec_ras_results/improved_results.json.
5. Write ~/Documents/hec_ras_results/scenario_comparison.csv with columns: scenario,peak_wse_ft,mean_peak_wse_ft,inundated_cells,total_cells,flood_reduction_pct (header + 2 data rows: baseline, improved). flood_reduction_pct = 100*(baseline_inundated - improved_inundated)/baseline_inundated, rounded to 1 decimal.
6. Write ~/Documents/hec_ras_results/project_benefit_summary.txt: a 5+ sentence technical summary stating the existing and improved peak WSE, the WSE reduction achieved, the change in number of inundated cells, the percent reduction in flood extent, and a recommendation on whether the project meets the 0.3 ft WSE-reduction design criterion.

Note: Run command: RasUnsteady Muncie.p04.tmp.hdf x04. Results are in Muncie.p04.hdf.
